notes.title: 1 · Flatten outputs
notes.text: Retain the Python output structure; flatten its leaves. A string leaf is rejected because unpacking a dict into its keys is usually a mistake.

notes.title: 2 · Normalize values and chains
notes.text: Convert leaves to Graph Values and include final chain values when the graph has chain inputs. Chains preserve dependency ordering.

notes.title: 3 · Set both signatures
notes.text: The actual argument and result types define functionType and the kgen generator signature. Symbolic dimensions can remain symbolic.

notes.title: 4 · Append the terminator
notes.text: mo.output identifies which SSA values leave the graph. This records IR; it does not launch inference.

notes.title: 5 · Name the interface
notes.text: Ordinal input/result names are written for the engine. The Python output tree is retained separately.

notes.title: 6 · Verify the graph
notes.text: Clear temporary bookkeeping and invoke MLIR graph verification. Failure reports diagnostics. Numerical correctness and target compilation remain separate checks.

graph_output.label: Finish the graph's output contract and verify the completed graph.

lessons.title: Follow one operation all the way through
lessons.detail: Select an operation or its loads/stores. Follow its source ancestry, changing representations, cache route, compiled code and two calls to the retained model.
lessons.ascii:
Python builder + Mojo package → verified G1
G1 retained → compiler clone C1 → artifact lookup
miss: MO → MAP → MOGG → MGP → kernel lookup
kernel miss: specialize Mojo → LLVM → target code
compiled routines → runtime callables → CM1 / MEF bytes
artifact hit: reuse CM1; kernel hit: reuse code, prepare graph
S1.init(CM1) → M1 → execute(B1) → O1 ready
Same S1 / M1 / code → execute(B2) → O2 ready

lessons.title: From Bazel's build graph to a selected device backend
lessons.detail: Follow the build/run boundary, each MAX dialect conversion, concrete Mojo specialization, target selection and initialized execution. Text retains the complete previous answers 1–7 and expands their numbered details; each animation step links to its explanation.
lessons.ascii:
1 · ./bazelw build //max/examples/custom_ops:addition
    Python launcher + runfiles; kernels/*.mojo is data
    Mojo library dependencies → separate .mojoc packages
2 · ./bazelw run //max/examples/custom_ops:addition
    Graph(custom_extensions=kernels/) → mojo precompile subprocess
    private staging .mojoc → atomic publication → package P1
    Python entry point stays separate; G1 records shape/dtype/device
3 · InferenceSession.compile(G1); caller retains G1
    C1 / MO: Modular Operations · typed tensor graph
      MOToMAPPass + MojoRegistry → access/kernel structure
    C1 / MAP: Modular Access Primitives · load/compute/store + fusion
      MAPToMOGGPass + MAPToMOGGState → generator/routine calls
    C1 / MOGG: Modular Operation Generator Graph
      MOGGToMGPPass + MOGraphLowering → init/execute resources
    C1 / MGP: Modular Glue Primitives · buffers/dependencies/state
    Device-graph finalization: audit only when getIsDeviceGraph()
4 · EmitMojo → separate KIR1; C1 retains the MGP plan
    kernel JIT miss → KGENCompiler.runElaborationPipeline
    generators + target/dtype/parameters → concrete KGEN / POP
    ObjectCompiler + buildLowerToLLVMPipeline → LLVM dialect (MLIR)
    mlir::translateModuleToLLVMIR → LLVM1 / llvm::Module
5 · TargetInfo triple/arch/features → TargetBackendRegistry lookup
    LLVM TargetRegistry → LLVM TargetMachine
    CPU: HostBackend → host object → linked native code
    NVIDIA: nvptx64-nvidia-cuda / sm_90a → PTX
      CUDA CompilationDevice.compileFunction → same-SM cubin
    AMD: amdgcn-amd-amdhsa / gfx942 + required device bitcode
      AMDGPU object → device ELF link → hsaco
6 · Host Python/MAX/driver stays on CPU; device kernels have their own target
    LowerCompiledRoutines → ModuleLoad / ExecuteGeneric
    prepared CM1 / MEF bytes → session.init → executable M1
    M1 + numerical Buffers → native execution → result readiness
7 · Native MLIR/LLVM APIs run compiler passes in the process
    No standalone mlir-opt command is part of these example targets
    IR/dump names are teaching views; GPU architectures are source-test examples

lessons.title: Follow one operation all the way through
lessons.detail: Select an operation or its loads/stores. Follow its source ancestry, changing representations, cache route, compiled code and two calls to the retained model.
lessons.ascii:
Python builder + Mojo package → verified G1
G1 retained → compiler clone C1 → artifact lookup
miss: MO → MAP → MOGG → MGP → kernel lookup
kernel miss: specialize Mojo → LLVM → target code
compiled routines → runtime callables → CM1 / MEF bytes
artifact hit: reuse CM1; kernel hit: reuse code, prepare graph
S1.init(CM1) → M1 → execute(B1) → O1 ready
Same S1 / M1 / code → execute(B2) → O2 ready

lessons.title: From Bazel's build graph to a selected device backend
lessons.detail: Follow the build/run boundary, each MAX dialect conversion, concrete Mojo specialization, target selection and initialized execution. Text retains the complete previous answers 1–7 and expands their numbered details; each animation step links to its explanation.
lessons.ascii:
1 · ./bazelw build //max/examples/custom_ops:elementwise_addition
    Python launcher + runfiles; kernels/*.mojo is data
    Mojo library dependencies → separate .mojoc packages
2 · ./bazelw run //max/examples/custom_ops:elementwise_addition
    Graph(custom_extensions=kernels/) → mojo precompile subprocess
    private staging .mojoc → atomic publication → package P1
    Python entry point stays separate; G1 records shape/dtype/device
3 · InferenceSession.compile(G1); caller retains G1
    C1 / MO: Modular Operations · typed tensor graph
      MOToMAPPass + MojoRegistry → access/kernel structure
    C1 / MAP: Modular Access Primitives · load/compute/store + fusion
      MAPToMOGGPass + MAPToMOGGState → generator/routine calls
    C1 / MOGG: Modular Operation Generator Graph
      MOGGToMGPPass + MOGraphLowering → init/execute resources
    C1 / MGP: Modular Glue Primitives · buffers/dependencies/state
    Device-graph finalization: audit only when getIsDeviceGraph()
4 · EmitMojo → separate KIR1; C1 retains the MGP plan
    kernel JIT miss → KGENCompiler.runElaborationPipeline
    generators + target/dtype/parameters → concrete KGEN / POP
    ObjectCompiler + buildLowerToLLVMPipeline → LLVM dialect (MLIR)
    mlir::translateModuleToLLVMIR → LLVM1 / llvm::Module
5 · TargetInfo triple/arch/features → TargetBackendRegistry lookup
    LLVM TargetRegistry → LLVM TargetMachine
    CPU: HostBackend → host object → linked native code
    NVIDIA: nvptx64-nvidia-cuda / sm_90a → PTX
      CUDA CompilationDevice.compileFunction → same-SM cubin
    AMD: amdgcn-amd-amdhsa / gfx942 + required device bitcode
      AMDGPU object → device ELF link → hsaco
6 · Host Python/MAX/driver stays on CPU; device kernels have their own target
    LowerCompiledRoutines → ModuleLoad / ExecuteGeneric
    prepared CM1 / MEF bytes → session.init → executable M1
    M1 + numerical Buffers → native execution → result readiness
7 · Native MLIR/LLVM APIs run compiler passes in the process
    No standalone mlir-opt command is part of these example targets
    IR/dump names are teaching views; GPU architectures are source-test examples

example.title: Choose a kernel. Coordinate its tiles.
example.expression: C = A @ B; algorithm is a compile-time parameter
example.subtitle: Follow target specialization, global/shared storage and two different readiness gates.
example.tiny: Tiny view: A [2,4], B [4,2], BK=2; original: M=K=N=256
example.notes: Original tiled BM=BN=BK is 32 on non-AMD GPUs and 16 on AMD. Main tests several GPU algorithms and a later 128×256×384 case; CPU main uses naive. Each helper call compiles and initializes its own model while reusing the session. The final expected assignment is a@b, overwriting the earlier fp64 reference.

graph_init.purpose: Create MLIR graph structure and optionally trace a Python callable.

notes.title: Symbolic dimensions
notes.text: Names from symbolic tensor/buffer dimensions become graph parameters.

notes.title: MLIR ownership
notes.text: Use a supplied module or create one, then create mo.graph with input types and initially empty result types.

notes.title: Kernel declarations and graph mode
notes.text: Import the kernel library and mark the graph if explicit device-graph construction was requested.

notes.title: Automatic finalization
notes.text: Run the callable inside the active graph context. Its return form determines how output is invoked.

graph_init.label: Create MLIR graph structure and optionally trace a Python callable.

graph_output.purpose: Finish the graph's output contract and verify the completed graph.

notes.title: 1 · Flatten outputs
notes.text: Retain the Python output structure; flatten its leaves. A string leaf is rejected because unpacking a dict into its keys is usually a mistake.

notes.title: 2 · Normalize values and chains
notes.text: Convert leaves to Graph Values and include final chain values when the graph has chain inputs. Chains preserve dependency ordering.

notes.title: 3 · Set both signatures
notes.text: The actual argument and result types define functionType and the kgen generator signature. Symbolic dimensions can remain symbolic.

notes.title: 4 · Append the terminator
notes.text: mo.output identifies which SSA values leave the graph. This records IR; it does not launch inference.

notes.title: 5 · Name the interface
notes.text: Ordinal input/result names are written for the engine. The Python output tree is retained separately.

notes.title: 6 · Verify the graph
notes.text: Clear temporary bookkeeping and invoke MLIR graph verification. Failure reports diagnostics. Numerical correctness and target compilation remain separate checks.

graph_output.label: Finish the graph's output contract and verify the completed graph.

frontend.purpose: Clone the graph module, configure lowering, and consult the native MEF cache.

notes.title: Compiler-owned module
notes.text: Lowering transforms a clone of the incoming module. Weight resources are owned by its MLIR context.

notes.title: Resolve compiler options
notes.text: Collect configuration and detect pre-seeded kernel declarations before deriving cache behavior.

notes.title: Cache-hit return
notes.text: When model-IR caching is enabled and a matching artifact exists, return it before convertMOToMEF runs.

notes.title: Cache miss
notes.text: Compile/serialize, then attempt to insert the resulting buffer in the cache.

frontend.label: Clone the graph module, configure lowering, and consult the native MEF cache.

mo_pipeline.purpose: Prepare and optimize high-level graph operations before MAP lowering.

notes.title: Kernel definitions
notes.text: Import/verify packages only when declarations were not already seeded by the caller.

notes.title: Shape and symbolic work
notes.text: Shape inference and constant folding are configured independently; symbolic optimization and cleanup run in this stage.

notes.title: Layouts and optional patterns
notes.text: Infer layouts and optionally run named pattern fusion before validating device information.

notes.title: Target legality
notes.text: Check device information before the final cleanup and unused-operation removal.

mo_pipeline.label: Prepare and optimize high-level graph operations before MAP lowering.

map_pipeline.purpose: Fuse eligible structured computations and outline kernel bodies.

notes.title: Structural fusion
notes.text: Fusion is a transformation of eligible graph structure. The schedule alone does not prove which Llama operations fuse.

notes.title: Output storage
notes.text: Provide accumulating buffers after fusion, including mixed-precision handling.

notes.title: Outline bodies
notes.text: Create structured kernel bodies after view handling, then simplify their captures and invariant views.

map_pipeline.label: Fuse eligible structured computations and outline kernel bodies.

mogg_pipeline.purpose: Legalize kernel calls and outline routines.

notes.title: Call preparation
notes.text: Legalize rowwise kernels, conform operands, outline routines, and add tracing wrappers before module cleanup.

mogg_pipeline.label: Legalize kernel calls and outline routines.

mgp_pipeline.purpose: Plan runtime resources, lower primitives, and emit Mojo routines.

notes.title: Memory planning
notes.text: Buffer reuse, allocation planning, deferral, and argument validation operate on the runtime-model representation.

notes.title: Device-graph path
notes.text: Staging, dependency computation, build stubs, and finalization are separate from the frontend Graph.output operation.

notes.title: Deduplicate routines
notes.text: Earlier canonicalization makes equivalent routines eligible for merging. Layer count is not necessarily the count of distinct generated routines.

notes.title: Emit source for JIT
notes.text: Mojo emission is at the end of this builder. The enclosing pipeline schedules kernel JIT afterward.

mgp_pipeline.label: Plan runtime resources, lower primitives, and emit Mojo routines.

gc_pipeline.purpose: Build the ordered sequence of representation conversions and compiler stages.

notes.title: High-level graph stage
notes.text: The mo-pre-map dump follows MO processing; subsequent stage names distinguish conversions from stage-local transforms.

notes.title: Representation transition
notes.text: Stable-tensor marking precedes MO-to-MAP conversion.

notes.title: Kernel representation
notes.text: MOGG preparation precedes conversion into the MGP runtime model.

notes.title: JIT configuration
notes.text: JIT target and compilation options are only configured when JIT is enabled.

notes.title: Compile kernels
notes.text: After MGP/Mojo emission, run JIT compilation, strip kernel declarations, and finish runtime-call lowering.

gc_pipeline.label: Build the ordered sequence of representation conversions and compiler stages.
